```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(psych)
library(knitr)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 16))

# Cleaned data from IC10-2-1 (Data Preparation)
case31 <- read_sav("Case31_Data_efcu_JE_cleaned.sav")

# Frequency table: count and percent, value labels shown
freq_table <- function(data, var) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ var }})) |>
    mutate(response = as_factor({{ var }}, levels = "labels")) |>
    count(response, .drop = FALSE) |>
    mutate(percent = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))
}

# Bar chart of response frequencies
freq_bar <- function(data, var, x_lab, title) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ var }})) |>
    mutate(response = as_factor({{ var }}, levels = "labels")) |>
    ggplot(aes(response, fill = response)) +
    geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = x_lab, y = "# of Responses", title = title)
}

# One-sample t-test (mu = 3, the scale midpoint) as a one-row table
t_row <- function(data, var, label) {
  x <- data[[var]]
  res <- t.test(x, mu = 3)
  tibble(
    Variable = label,
    n = sum(!is.na(x)),
    Mean = round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD = round(sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    t = round(unname(res$statistic), 2),
    df = unname(res$parameter),
    p = format.pval(res$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
  )
}

# Chi-square goodness-of-fit test against equal proportions as a one-row table
gof_row <- function(data, var, label) {
  levs <- setdiff(levels(as_factor(data[[var]], levels = "labels")), "No answer")
  x <- as.character(as_factor(data[[var]], levels = "labels"))
  tab <- table(factor(x[!is.na(x)], levels = levs))
  res <- chisq.test(tab, p = rep(1 / length(tab), length(tab)))
  tibble(
    Variable = label,
    Observed = paste(names(tab), tab, sep = ": ", collapse = " | "),
    `Chi-sq` = round(unname(res$statistic), 2),
    df = unname(res$parameter),
    `Min. expected` = round(min(res$expected), 1),
    p = format.pval(res$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
  )
}
```

# Data {background-color="#a13c65"}

## Data Used

-   **Data:** `Case31_Data_efcu_JE_cleaned.sav`, the cleaned file from IC10-2-1 (Data Preparation)
-   **Participants:** `r nrow(case31)` members
-   **Coding used in this analysis:**
    -   "No opinion" (q7, q8, q37) and "No answer" (q12) were set to missing
    -   q7r, q8r, q10r, and q37r are reverse coded so a larger number = a higher rating
    -   q13r-q26r: 1 = Unaware, 2 = Aware but Have Not Used, 3 = Aware and Have Used
    -   q9_group: statement frequency grouped into too often / about right / not often enough
-   **Decision rule:** reject H~0~ when *p* \< .05

# R1: One-Sample t-test {background-color="aquamarine"}

**R1: Why do people join the Credit Union?**

-   `Constructs and roles`: Reasons why people join the Credit Union (descriptive)
-   `Operationalization`: q7r (opinion on the rates CU pays on share/savings accounts)
-   `Scale`: 1-5 point, Likert-type scale (1 = Very Low ... 5 = Very High)
-   `Statistics`: Descriptive statistics, followed by one-sample t-test

## Descriptive Statistics

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-q7r-freq
#| tbl-cap: Response Frequency of Savings Rate (q7r)

case31 |>
  freq_table(q7r) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Savings Rate", "n", "%"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-q7r-desc
#| tbl-cap: Descriptive Statistics for Savings Rate (q7r)

describe(case31$q7r) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(n, mean, sd, median, min, max, skew, kurtosis) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  kable()
```
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}

case31 |>
  freq_bar(q7r, "Savings Rate", "Member Opinions on Savings Rates (q7r)")
```

::::

## One-Sample t-test

-   H~0~: μ = 3 (members rate the savings rate as "Average")
-   H~A~: μ ≠ 3

```{r}
#| echo: true

t.test(case31$q7r, mu = 3)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
r1 <- t_row(case31, "q7r", "q7r")
pct_avg_q7r <- case31 |> freq_table(q7r) |> filter(response == "Average") |> pull(percent)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Insights about R1

-   Most members (`r pct_avg_q7r`%) rate the savings rate the CU pays as "Average."
-   The sample mean (*M* = `r r1$Mean`) is not statistically different from 3 ("Average") (*t*(`r r1$df`) = `r r1$t`, *p* = `r r1$p`).
-   Members see the CU's savings rate as about average, so higher savings rates are not a strong reason to join or stay with the CU.
:::

-   H~A~: μ ≠ 3

```{r}
r2 <- bind_rows(
  t_row(case31, "q8r", "q8r: Loan rates charged"),
  t_row(case31, "q30", "q30: CU loan rates lower")
)
r2 |> kable(caption = "One-Sample t-test Results for R2 (test value = 3)")

pct_avg_q8r <- case31 |> freq_table(q8r) |> filter(response == "Average") |> pull(percent)
pct_unc_q30 <- case31 |> freq_table(q30) |> filter(response == "Uncertain") |> pull(percent)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Insights about R2

-   Most members rate the CU's loan rates as "Average" (`r pct_avg_q8r`%). The mean (*M* = `r r2$Mean[1]`) is not statistically different from 3 (*p* = `r r2$p[1]`).
-   On whether CU loan rates are lower than other institutions, the most common answer is "Uncertain" (`r pct_unc_q30`%). The mean (*M* = `r r2$Mean[2]`) is not statistically different from 3 (*p* = `r r2$p[2]`).
-   Members do not see the CU's loans as cheaper than other lenders. With no rate advantage, members have little reason to borrow from the CU instead of other institutions.
:::

# R5: Chi-square Goodness-of-Fit {background-color="aquamarine"}

**R5: How well are the members aware of the services offered by the credit union?**

-   `Constructs and roles`: Awareness of services (descriptive)
-   `Operationalization`: q13r-q26r (14 services)
-   `Scale`: Ordinal scale (1 = Unaware, 2 = Aware but Have Not Used, 3 = Aware and Have Used)
-   `Statistics`: Descriptive statistics (frequency distribution), followed by chi-square goodness-of-fit test

```{r}
services <- c(
  q13r = "Regular share accounts", q14r = "Special subaccounts",
  q15r = "Christmas club accounts", q16r = "Individual retirement accounts",
  q17r = "MasterCard credit cards", q18r = "Signature loans",
  q19r = "New car loans", q20r = "Late model car loans",
  q21r = "Older model car loans", q22r = "Household goods/appliance loans",
  q23r = "Recreational loans", q24r = "Share collateralized loans",
  q25r = "IRA loans", q26r = "Line of credit loans"
)

awareness_long <- case31 |>
  select(all_of(names(services))) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) as_factor(x, levels = "labels"))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "aware_level") |>
  mutate(service = factor(services[variable], levels = services))
```

## Frequency Distribution

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r5-freq
#| tbl-cap: Awareness of Services, % of Members (n = 128)

awareness_long |>
  count(service, aware_level, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(service) |>
  mutate(percent = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = aware_level, values_from = percent) |>
  rename(Service = service) |>
  kable()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
#| label: fig-r5-bar
#| fig-cap: Awareness Levels Across CU Services
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 7.5

awareness_long |>
  count(service, aware_level) |>
  group_by(service) |>
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(percent, fct_rev(service), fill = aware_level)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "% of Members", y = NULL, fill = "Awareness",
       title = "Members' Awareness of CU Services (q13r-q26r)") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Chi-square Goodness-of-Fit Tests

-   H~0~: The awareness levels follow the expected (equal, 1/3 each) distribution
-   H~A~: The awareness levels do not follow the expected distribution

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Example: regular share accounts (q13r)
table(as_factor(case31$q13r)) |>
  chisq.test(p = c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r5-gof
#| tbl-cap: Chi-square Goodness-of-Fit Tests for All 14 Services (expected = 1/3 per level)

r5 <- map2(names(services), services, \(v, lab) gof_row(case31, v, lab)) |>
  list_rbind()
r5 |> kable()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
top_level <- awareness_long |>
  count(service, aware_level) |>
  group_by(service) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()

used_pct <- awareness_long |>
  group_by(service) |>
  summarise(used = round(mean(aware_level == "Aware and Have Used") * 100, 1))

n_aware_not_used <- sum(top_level$aware_level == "Aware but Have Not Used")
unaware_top <- top_level |> filter(aware_level == "Unaware") |> pull(service) |> as.character()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Insights about R5

-   For all 14 services, the awareness levels are significantly different from an equal distribution (all *p* \< .001). The expected count is 42.7 in every cell, so the tests are valid.
-   For `r n_aware_not_used` of the 14 services, the most common answer is "Aware but Have Not Used." Members know about most of the loan products but are not using them (e.g., signature loans: `r used_pct$used[used_pct$service == "Signature loans"]`% have used; new car loans: `r used_pct$used[used_pct$service == "New car loans"]`%).
-   "Unaware" is the most common answer for `r paste(unaware_top, collapse = ", ")`.
-   Use is low across the board. Only MasterCard credit cards (`r used_pct$used[used_pct$service == "MasterCard credit cards"]`%) and line of credit loans (`r used_pct$used[used_pct$service == "Line of credit loans"]`%) are used by more than a third of members.
-   The CU should raise awareness of its lesser-known services and give members reasons to actually use the loan products they already know about.
:::

## Statements: Chi-square Goodness-of-Fit Tests

-   H~0~: Responses follow the expected (equal) distribution
-   H~A~: Responses do not follow the expected distribution

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Example: statements easy to understand (q11), expected 50% / 50%
table(droplevels(as_factor(case31$q11))) |>
  chisq.test(p = c(.5, .5))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-gof
#| tbl-cap: Chi-square Goodness-of-Fit Tests (expected = equal proportions)

r6_gof <- bind_rows(
  gof_row(case31, "q9_group", "q9_group: Statement frequency"),
  gof_row(case31, "q10r", "q10r: Statement accuracy"),
  gof_row(case31, "q11", "q11: Easy to understand"),
  gof_row(case31, "q12", "q12: Info kept confidential")

r6_gof |> kable()
```

## Attitudes and Overall Rating: Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
r6_items <- c(
  q31 = "q31: Personal financial info kept confidential",
  q32 = "q32: Prompt in processing loan applications",
  q33 = "q33: Services meet members' needs",
  q34 = "q34: Loan applications simple and easy",
  q37r = "q37r: Overall management and operation"
)
```

:::: columns
::: {.column width="45%"}

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: Descriptive Statistics for q31-q34 and q37r

describe(case31[names(r6_items)]) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "Variable") |>
  select(Variable, n, mean, sd, median, min, max) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  kable()
```

q31-q34: 1 = Strongly Disagree ... 5 = Strongly Agree. q37r: 1 = Very Poor ... 5 = Excellent. q31-q34 are tested as separate items because their reliability in IC10-2-1 was too low to combine them into an index.
:::

```{r}
  group_by(variable) |>

  mutate(item = factor(r6_items[variable], levels = rev(r6_items))) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, item)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
```

## One-Sample t-tests

-   H~0~: μ = 3 (q31-q34: "Uncertain"; q37r: "Average")
-   H~A~: μ ≠ 3

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Example: overall rating of management and operation (q37r)
t.test(case31$q37r, mu = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-t
#| tbl-cap: One-Sample t-test Results for R6 (test value = 3)

r6_t <- map2(names(r6_items), r6_items, \(v, lab) t_row(case31, v, lab)) |>
  list_rbind()
r6_t |> kable()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
pct <- function(var, level) {
  case31 |> freq_table({{ var }}) |> filter(response != "No answer") |>
    mutate(percent = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) |>
    filter(response == level) |> pull(percent)
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Insights about R6

-   **Statements:** Most members say statement frequency is "About right" (`r pct(q9_group, "About right")`%), and no one says "Too often." Most rate accuracy as "Good" or "Excellent" (`r pct(q10r, "Good") + pct(q10r, "Excellent")`%), and almost all find statements easy to understand (`r pct(q11, "Yes")`%). All four distributions differ significantly from equal proportions (*p* \< .001).
-   **Confidentiality:** `r pct(q12, "Yes")`% say the CU keeps account information confidential (q12, *p* \< .001), and q31 has the highest agreement of the four attitude items (*M* = `r r6_t$Mean[1]`).
-   **Loan processing and services:** Members agree, but less strongly, that loan applications are processed promptly (*M* = `r r6_t$Mean[2]`), services meet their needs (*M* = `r r6_t$Mean[3]`), and loan applications are simple and easy (*M* = `r r6_t$Mean[4]`). All are significantly above 3 (*p* \< .001), but loan applications have the lowest score.
-   **Overall:** Members rate the CU's management and operation as good (*M* = `r r6_t$Mean[5]`, *p* \< .001).
-   Members believe the CU is run effectively. Loan applications score lowest, so making them simpler could help the CU's borrowing problem.
:::
